result: SUMOylation of PCNA is required for telomere elongation in elg1Δ mutants. Single mutations at K127R or K164R in PCNA have little effect on telomere length by themselves or in elg1Δ, but mutating both lysines (pol30-RR) completely abrogates the long telomere phenotype of elg1Δ. Deletion of RAD18 (ubiquitin ligase) has no effect on elg1Δ telomeres. Overexpression of wild-type PCNA or PCNA-SUMO fusion causes telomere elongation, but overexpression of unmodifiable pol30-RR or PCNA-ubiquitin fusion does not.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the genetic data showing PCNA SUMOylation is required for elg1Δ telomere elongation, but express significant doubt about the claim that SUMO-PCNA acts as a positive signal for telomerase activation. One reviewer states 'the data do not convincingly support the claim that SUMO-PCNA is a positive signal for telomerase activation,' and another notes that 'telomeres in pol30-RR strains are normal length,' suggesting the interactions are 'not necessary for telomerase activation.' The data show correlation but reviewers question the mechanistic interpretation.

result: Elg1 and Stn1 work in the same telomere length maintenance pathway. Double mutants elg1Δ stn1-13 and elg1Δ stn1-164 show epistasis, with telomeres not longer than single mutants, indicating both proteins function in the same pathway.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the epistasis data as evidence that Elg1 and Stn1 work in the same pathway. One reviewer explicitly states 'the double mutants of Elg1 and Stn1 do not show increased telomere length phenotype in comparison to the single mutants, indicating that both proteins work in the same pathway.' This genetic interaction is treated as solid evidence for pathway placement.

result: Elg1 physically interacts with Stn1 but not with Cdc13 or Ten1. Co-immunoprecipitation of epitope-tagged Elg1 pulled down Stn1 but not Cdc13 or Ten1. This interaction occurs exclusively during late S-phase and is direct.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge these physical interaction data as a strength of the paper. One reviewer notes 'the strength of the paper is in the observations of new interactions between CST, Elg1, and PCNA' and another states 'the interaction between Elg1 and Stn1 seems direct and occurs exclusively during the late S-phase.' The co-IP data are accepted as demonstrating these interactions.

result: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of Elg1 interacts with CST components in yeast two-hybrid assays. Elg1-NTD interacts strongly with Cdc13 and Stn1, and weakly with Ten1. The C-terminal domain shows no interaction. The interaction with Stn1 is abolished when SIM motifs are mutated, but the interaction with Cdc13 is not affected by SIM mutations in the plasmid-borne NTD.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the yeast two-hybrid data showing these domain-specific interactions. The differential dependence on SIM motifs for Stn1 versus Cdc13 interactions is noted as part of the experimental findings. These data contribute to the overall picture of 'interesting physical connections between Elg1 and CST proteins' that reviewers acknowledge.

result: SUMO modifications differentially regulate Elg1-CST interactions. Deletion of SUMO ligases SIZ1/SIZ2 abolishes interactions between Elg1-NTD and both Stn1 and Cdc13. The Elg1-Stn1 interaction persists in pol30-RR background (no PCNA SUMOylation) and is independent of PCNA SUMOylation. In contrast, the Elg1-Cdc13 interaction requires PCNA SUMOylation, and Cdc13 physically interacts with PCNA in a SUMOylation-dependent manner.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these differential dependencies on SUMOylation as demonstrated by the yeast two-hybrid and co-IP experiments. The data showing that Elg1-Stn1 interaction is independent of PCNA SUMOylation while Elg1-Cdc13 interaction depends on it are acknowledged as part of the experimental findings characterizing 'interactions that appear to be modulated by sumolyation.'

result: The Elg1-Cdc13 interaction requires genomic ELG1 and PCNA unloading activity. In elg1Δ strains, plasmid-borne Elg1-NTD fails to interact with Cdc13 but still interacts with Stn1. In strains with elg1 alleles lacking PCNA unloading activity (elg1-DD, elg1-sim+DD, elg1-WalkerA), the Elg1-NTD-Cdc13 interaction is abolished or greatly reduced. The interaction requires: (1) Cdc13 SUMOylation, (2) PCNA SUMOylation, and (3) PCNA unloading capability.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge the yeast two-hybrid data showing these dependencies, they express uncertainty about the mechanistic interpretation. The conclusion that the Elg1-Cdc13 interaction is 'indirect and can only take place after PCNA has been SUMOylated and unloaded' is part of the model that reviewers find 'not yet convincingly demonstrated.' One reviewer notes 'the detailed choreography of the events as well as the role of PCNA-SUMO remain elusive.'

result: SUMOylation of Cdc13 is required for its interaction with Elg1. Preventing SUMOylation of Cdc13 using cdc13-snm mutant abolishes the interaction between Cdc13 and Elg1 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the experimental data characterizing the SUMO-dependent interactions. The requirement for Cdc13 SUMOylation is acknowledged as one of the conditions necessary for the Elg1-Cdc13 interaction, consistent with the overall theme of SUMO-mediated regulation.

result: Elg1-Stn1 interaction occurs specifically during late S-phase when telomeres are replicated. Co-IP experiments show Pol3 interacts with Elg1 during S-phase (40-70 min, 120-140 min), while Stn1 is detected only in late S-phase (60-70 min, 140-160 min). PCNA arrival at telomeres (60-70 min) coincides with Elg1-Stn1 interaction timing.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the cell cycle timing data from co-IP and ChIP experiments. One reviewer explicitly states 'the interaction between Elg1 and Stn1 seems direct and occurs exclusively during the late S-phase.' The temporal correlation with telomerase activity and PCNA localization is acknowledged as part of the experimental findings.

result: Elg1 facilitates the Stn1-Cdc13 interaction. In elg1Δ strains, Stn1 shows strongly reduced co-precipitation with Cdc13, suggesting the Stn1-Cdc13 interaction is at least partly dependent on Elg1.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this co-IP data showing reduced Stn1-Cdc13 interaction in the absence of Elg1. This finding is consistent with the overall model that Elg1 plays a role in coordinating CST complex assembly, though reviewers question the broader mechanistic interpretation of how this relates to telomerase regulation.

result: The authors propose a model where SUMOylated PCNA serves as a positive signal for telomerase activity, and Elg1-mediated PCNA unloading coordinates the switch from telomerase activation to termination. The model suggests: (1) SUMOylated PCNA arrival activates telomerase, (2) Elg1 interacts with Stn1 at telomeres, (3) Elg1-Stn1 unloads SUMO-PCNA, (4) Cdc13 becomes SUMOylated, (5) the complete CST complex forms and terminates telomerase activity.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state this model is not convincingly demonstrated. One reviewer notes 'the data do not convincingly support the claim that SUMO-PCNA is a positive signal for telomerase activation' and 'the model may be correct but it is not yet convincingly demonstrated.' Another reviewer points out that 'telomeres in pol30-RR strains are normal length,' indicating the proposed mechanism is 'not necessary for telomerase activation or inhibition.' A third reviewer states 'the detailed choreography of the events as well as the role of PCNA-SUMO remain elusive' and notes the model 'makes some assumptions that are not demonstrated by this work.'

result: The authors propose that SUMOylated PCNA is only needed for 'sustained' telomerase activity, not 'basal' activity. They note pol30-RR mutants have normal-sized telomeres despite lacking PCNA SUMOylation, and suggest this supports a two-mode model of telomerase where SUMO-PCNA is required only for the sustained mode.
evaluation: Reviewers note the observation that pol30-RR mutants have normal telomeres as evidence against the necessity of SUMO-PCNA for telomerase function, but do not explicitly evaluate the two-mode interpretation. One reviewer uses this observation to question the model: 'telomeres in pol30-RR strains are normal length,' suggesting the proposed interactions are 'not necessary for telomerase activation.' The interpretation remains speculative and not fully supported.

result: Elg1-NTD interacts with the C-terminal domain of Stn1 in both wild-type and elg1Δ strains. Both Elg1 and Cdc13 bind Stn1 at its C-terminus.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these domain mapping data from yeast two-hybrid experiments as part of the characterization of the physical interactions. These findings contribute to understanding the molecular basis of the Elg1-Stn1 interaction.
